title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
gist: Review of the Asus ProArt P16 built on Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark N1X with up to 128GB unified memory (~110GB usable for AI on Windows), which can run 100B+ parameter models locally. The author finds local agents work but are slow (Qwen 27B ~20 tokens/s, larger models a few tokens/s), battery drains in ~2 hours of inference, and at $6,999.99 it is a niche machine whose cost exceeds years of premium cloud AI subscriptions.

insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Nvidia is entering the Windows PC CPU market with an Arm SoC, a competitive threat to Intel, AMD and Qualcomm.

insights.claim: The RTX Spark laptop uses 128GB of shared LPDDR5x memory at up to 300GB/s, slower than a discrete GPU's GDDR7 but several times more capacity than any gaming GPU, letting it load models with 100+ billion parameters.

insights.so_what: Privacy and model-routing transparency are a potential wedge for local-AI hardware against cloud AI providers.

themes.theme: Local model performance and agent reliability

insights.claim: On the RTX Spark laptop, Qwen 27B generates about 20 tokens per second on simple tasks, Google's mid-weight Gemma models occasionally hit 40 tokens per second but drop to a quarter of that on complex tasks, and the 125-billion-parameter Qwen Flash Next manages only a few tokens per second.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Local inference remains materially slower than cloud frontier models, limiting displacement of cloud AI.
insights.locator: With simple tasks, models like Qwen 27B

insights.claim: The reviewer judges Chinese model Qwen to be the best option currently for local AI, despite political censorship caveats.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight models are leading the local-AI ecosystem, a competitive signal for US open-model efforts.
insights.quote: As long as you don’t need to ask it if Taiwan is a country, Qwen seems like the best option for local AI currently.
insights.locator: With simple tasks, models like Qwen 27B

insights.claim: Local AI agents on Windows can control the entire PC, doing anything a user at the keyboard can, which creates real risks of agents deleting directories or exposing data.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Agent safety and permissions tooling is an emerging need as on-device agents gain system access.

themes.theme: Windows on Arm and gaming limitations

insights.claim: Windows on Arm has matured: the Prism emulator runs x86 and x64 programs well enough that users usually won't notice, and gaps like Google Drive and VPN apps now have native Arm versions.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Improved Arm compatibility weakens the x86 moat of Intel and AMD in Windows PCs.

insights.claim: Gaming on Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark is hampered by virtually no native Arm Windows games, emulation overhead, and anti-cheat systems that cannot be emulated, though Nvidia is working with Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, and Denuvo.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: x86 plus discrete GPU retains its gaming advantage, limiting Spark's appeal as an all-in-one machine.

insights.claim: The reviewer concludes an x86 system with a discrete GPU is better for gaming and a lighter laptop better for most buyers, making the RTX Spark ProArt P16 a niche product for fervent AI boosters.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Near-term volumes for Nvidia's Spark laptops are likely to be small.
